svg.text: The integrated MVP 2 system, now observable, secure, deployed with zero downtime and tested under load and chaos
Step 1 in detail: promote through the gated pipeline (CI must be green), then tag the release
All green? → ready for real users
CI green: lint, types, tests, coverage
No secrets in git · dependency scans pass
Data stays correct even when things fail
Tag v3.0.0 · CHANGELOG · ADRs (architecture decisions) · updated runbooks
Close by showing ADRs, contracts and pipeline
SLO: promised target (e.g. 95% respond in < 300 ms)
Runbook: the “what do I do when the alarm rings?” guide
Golden signals: latency, traffic, errors, saturation
Chaos: break something on purpose to see if it holds
Breaker: stops calling the failed service
Saga: if a step fails, undo the previous ones
MVP 1: the chef can cook the dish.
MVP 2: kitchen, waiters and cashier work together.
MVP 3: it opens to the public, ready for anything:
New menu, doors stay open → zero downtime
New menu flops → old menu back (rollback)
A chef is out, still serving → chaos
What do the metrics show? (DORA, SLOs)
Tell the system’s story like a professional
+ Corte 3 adds: certification and final project
Caution: the final release is judged on operability, not just features. If it can’t survive a killed service or a load spike, it is not production-grade.
